easy: A teacher or helper who shows students how something works by doing it in front of them.

ex.en: The science demonstrator mixed two liquids, and the cup started to bubble.
ex.ko: 과학 시연자가 두 액체를 섞자 컵에서 거품이 일기 시작했다.

easy: A huge amount of computer data, about a billion billion bytes.

ex.en: All the videos on the internet take up many exabytes of space.
ex.ko: 인터넷에 있는 모든 동영상은 엑사바이트 단위의 엄청난 공간을 차지한다.

easy: A way of joining computers with cables so they can share information.

ex.en: Dad plugged an ethernet cable into the computer to make the internet faster.
ex.ko: 아빠가 인터넷을 더 빠르게 하려고 컴퓨터에 이더넷 케이블을 꽂았다.

easy: When one country sends a person accused of a crime back to another country to go to court there.

ex.en: After his extradition, the thief had to face a judge in his home country.
ex.ko: 송환된 뒤 그 도둑은 자기 나라에서 재판을 받아야 했다.

easy: How well you can see with your eyes.

ex.en: Grandma got new glasses because her eyesight was getting worse.
ex.ko: 할머니는 시력이 나빠져서 새 안경을 맞추셨다.

easy: About a generation, a group of people born around the same time, like kids, parents, and grandparents.

ex.en: There is a generational difference in how Grandpa and I use phones.
ex.ko: 할아버지와 내가 휴대폰을 쓰는 방식에는 세대 차이가 있다.

easy: Able to switch places without changing the answer or meaning.

ex.en: In 2 + 3, the numbers are interchangeable, because 3 + 2 is the same.
ex.ko: 2 + 3에서 두 숫자는 서로 바꿀 수 있다. 3 + 2도 같기 때문이다.

easy: A piece of clothing that covers your leg, often from the knee to the ankle.

ex.en: She wore warm leggings under her skirt on the snowy day.
ex.ko: 눈 오는 날 그녀는 치마 아래에 따뜻한 레깅스를 입었다.

easy: Caring mostly about money and things, more than about people.

ex.en: The mercenary shop owner raised prices when the storm came.
ex.ko: 돈만 아는 가게 주인은 폭풍이 오자 값을 올렸다.

easy: A soldier who is paid to fight for a country that is not their own.

ex.en: The king hired mercenaries from far away to protect his castle.
ex.ko: 왕은 성을 지키려고 먼 곳에서 용병을 고용했다.

easy: Using very few things, colors, or shapes, in a very simple style.

ex.en: My aunt's minimalist room has only a bed, a lamp, and one plant.
ex.ko: 이모의 미니멀한 방에는 침대와 전등, 화분 하나뿐이다.

easy: To make someone go the wrong way or believe something that is not true.

ex.en: The old map misled us, and we ended up at the wrong lake.
ex.ko: 낡은 지도가 우리를 잘못 이끌어서 엉뚱한 호수에 도착했다.

easy: A short, well-known saying that gives advice or tells a truth about life.

ex.en: "Practice makes perfect" is a proverb my coach loves to say.
ex.ko: "연습이 완벽을 만든다"는 우리 코치님이 즐겨 말하는 속담이다.

easy: The part of sleep when your eyes move quickly and you have dreams.

ex.en: Most of my dreams happen during REM sleep.
ex.ko: 내 꿈은 대부분 렘수면 동안 꾼다.

easy: So wrong or shocking that people think badly of the person who did it.

ex.en: It was scandalous that the team captain cheated on the test.
ex.ko: 팀 주장이 시험에서 부정행위를 한 것은 충격적인 일이었다.

easy: A young man long ago who served a knight and helped him with his armor and horse.

ex.en: The squire polished the knight's shiny armor before the contest.
ex.ko: 종자는 시합 전에 기사의 반짝이는 갑옷을 닦았다.

easy: A casual, short word for a kind of work or business.

ex.en: My uncle has worked in the music biz for twenty years.
ex.ko: 삼촌은 음악 업계에서 20년 동안 일했다.

easy: A V-shaped stripe on a uniform sleeve that shows a soldier's rank.

ex.en: The sergeant had three chevrons sewn on his sleeve.
ex.ko: 그 중사는 소매에 V자 계급장 세 개를 달고 있었다.

easy: A doctor or other health worker who treats real patients instead of doing lab work.

ex.en: The clinician listened carefully to the boy's cough.
ex.ko: 임상의는 소년의 기침 소리를 주의 깊게 들었다.

easy: To put someone to death by nailing or tying them to a cross, as was done in ancient Rome.

ex.en: In ancient Rome, some criminals were crucified as a punishment.
ex.ko: 고대 로마에서는 일부 죄인을 벌로 십자가에 못 박았다.

easy: To force a leader, like a king, out of their job.

ex.en: The people deposed the cruel king and chose a new leader.
ex.ko: 백성들은 잔인한 왕을 폐위하고 새 지도자를 뽑았다.

easy: In Hindu and Buddhist teachings, the basic rules of how the world works and how to live rightly.

ex.en: The monk taught the children about dharma and being kind.
ex.ko: 스님은 아이들에게 다르마와 친절함에 대해 가르쳤다.

easy: A way of cleaning a liquid by letting tiny bits pass through a thin filter, like machines that clean blood.

ex.en: Grandpa goes to the hospital for dialysis three times a week.
ex.ko: 할아버지는 일주일에 세 번 병원에 투석을 받으러 가신다.

easy: Belonging to a division, a very large group of soldiers in an army.

ex.en: The divisional flag waved high over the army camp.
ex.ko: 사단 깃발이 군부대 위에서 높이 펄럭였다.

easy: The part of the US government that takes care of national parks, public land, and nature.

ex.en: The Department of the Interior runs Yellowstone National Park.
ex.ko: 미국 내무부는 옐로스톤 국립공원을 관리한다.

easy: The very end of your finger.

ex.en: I touched the cold snow with my fingertip.
ex.ko: 나는 손가락 끝으로 차가운 눈을 만져 보았다.

easy: How much shooting power an army, ship, or weapon has.

ex.en: The big battleship had more firepower than all the small boats together.
ex.ko: 그 큰 전함은 작은 배들을 다 합친 것보다 화력이 셌다.

easy: Very scary and horrible to look at.

ex.en: The zombie movie was too gruesome for my little brother.
ex.ko: 그 좀비 영화는 내 남동생에게 너무 끔찍했다.

easy: To give someone enough water to drink so their body stays healthy.

ex.en: Coach told us to hydrate with lots of water during the hot game.
ex.ko: 코치님은 더운 경기 중에 물을 많이 마셔 수분을 보충하라고 하셨다.

easy: A unit that measures how much light a lamp or flashlight gives off.

ex.en: This flashlight gives 500 lumens, so it lights up the whole tent.
ex.ko: 이 손전등은 500루멘이라서 텐트 전체를 밝힌다.

easy: A chemical that has just one oxygen atom in each tiny piece.

ex.en: Carbon monoxide is a dangerous gas that you cannot see or smell.
ex.ko: 일산화탄소는 눈에 보이지도 냄새도 나지 않는 위험한 가스다.

easy: To keep telling someone again and again to do something or that they did something wrong.

ex.en: My sister nags me to clean my side of the room.
ex.ko: 누나는 내 쪽 방을 치우라고 잔소리한다.

easy: A person who keeps complaining and telling others what they did wrong.

ex.en: Don't be a nag; I said I would feed the dog soon.
ex.ko: 잔소리 좀 그만해. 곧 개 밥 준다고 했잖아.

easy: In math, not making a straight line when you draw it on a graph.

ex.en: The curve on the graph shows a nonlinear pattern.
ex.ko: 그래프의 곡선은 비선형 패턴을 보여 준다.

easy: To go back to the usual, normal way.

ex.en: After the storm, life in our town slowly normalized.
ex.ko: 폭풍이 지나간 뒤 우리 마을의 생활은 천천히 정상화되었다.

easy: When something owned by the government is sold to private companies.

ex.en: The privatization of the railway meant a company ran the trains instead of the government.
ex.ko: 철도가 민영화되어 정부 대신 회사가 기차를 운영하게 되었다.

easy: Sharing or handing something out again in a new way.

ex.en: The teacher did a redistribution of crayons so every table had enough.
ex.ko: 선생님은 모든 책상에 충분하도록 크레용을 다시 나누어 주었다.

easy: About small religious or political groups, often ones that disagree with each other.

ex.en: The country had sectarian fights between two religious groups.
ex.ko: 그 나라에는 두 종교 집단 사이의 종파 갈등이 있었다.

easy: A hard, clear or white material found in sand and rocks, used to make glass.

ex.en: The little packet in my new shoes is full of silica to keep them dry.
ex.ko: 새 신발 속 작은 봉지에는 습기를 막는 실리카가 들어 있다.

easy: A strong worried feeling that is hard to explain.

ex.en: The teenager in the story was full of angst about growing up.
ex.ko: 이야기 속 십 대 소년은 어른이 되는 것에 대한 불안으로 가득했다.

easy: A small unit of computer information, made of 8 bits, enough for one letter.

ex.en: Each letter you type takes up about one byte of memory.
ex.ko: 타자로 치는 글자 하나는 약 1바이트의 메모리를 차지한다.

easy: A person who asks for something they say they have a right to, like money or a title.

ex.en: Three claimants said the lost puppy belonged to them.
ex.ko: 세 명의 요구자가 길 잃은 강아지가 자기 것이라고 주장했다.

easy: In Greek myths, a nymph who turned into a laurel tree to escape the god Apollo.

ex.en: In the myth, Daphne became a laurel tree just as Apollo reached her.
ex.ko: 신화에서 다프네는 아폴론이 닿는 순간 월계수로 변했다.

easy: To take all the water out of food so it keeps for a long time.

ex.en: We dehydrated apple slices to take on our camping trip.
ex.ko: 우리는 캠핑 갈 때 가져가려고 사과 조각을 말렸다.

easy: Left for a person to decide by their own judgment.

ex.en: The principal has discretionary money for special school trips.
ex.ko: 교장 선생님에게는 특별 현장 학습에 쓸 수 있는 재량 예산이 있다.

easy: Spreading news or ideas so many people can hear and talk about them.

ex.en: The dissemination of the safety rules helped every family get ready for the storm.
ex.ko: 안전 수칙이 널리 전파되어 모든 가족이 폭풍에 대비할 수 있었다.

easy: Inside your own country, not with other countries.

ex.en: These toys are made domestically, not overseas.
ex.ko: 이 장난감들은 해외가 아니라 국내에서 만들어진다.

easy: To cut lines or a picture into a hard surface like metal or glass.

ex.en: The artist etched a tiny bird onto the glass cup.
ex.ko: 화가는 유리컵에 작은 새를 새겨 넣었다.

easy: A dark brown animal, like a weasel, that lives in woods and gives off a bad smell when scared.

ex.en: The fitch hid in the bushes and sprayed a stinky smell at the fox.
ex.ko: 긴털족제비는 덤불에 숨어 여우에게 고약한 냄새를 뿜었다.

easy: The part of your body where your legs meet the bottom of your belly.

ex.en: The soccer player hurt a muscle in his groin and had to sit out.
ex.ko: 그 축구 선수는 사타구니 근육을 다쳐 경기에서 빠져야 했다.

easy: A big wasp that can give a very painful sting.

ex.en: A hornet built a paper nest under our porch roof.
ex.ko: 말벌이 우리 현관 지붕 밑에 종이 같은 집을 지었다.

easy: To place someone in an important job or group with a special ceremony.

ex.en: The famous pitcher was inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame.
ex.ko: 그 유명한 투수는 야구 명예의 전당에 정식으로 헌액되었다.

easy: When the air near the ground is cooler than the air above it, which can trap smog.

ex.en: An inversion kept the foggy air stuck over the city all morning.
ex.ko: 기온 역전 때문에 오전 내내 뿌연 공기가 도시 위에 갇혀 있었다.

easy: Closing a business by selling everything it owns to pay what it owes.

ex.en: The toy store went into liquidation and sold all its toys cheaply.
ex.ko: 장난감 가게가 청산에 들어가서 모든 장난감을 싸게 팔았다.

easy: A man who acts tough and strong to show off how manly he is.

ex.en: He acted like a macho, refusing to cry even when his foot hurt.
ex.ko: 그는 마초처럼 굴며 발이 아파도 울지 않으려 했다.

easy: A very small difference in meaning, feeling, or color.

ex.en: "Glad" and "thrilled" both mean happy, but there is a nuance between them.
ex.ko: "glad"와 "thrilled"는 둘 다 기쁘다는 뜻이지만 미묘한 차이가 있다.

easy: Following the old, accepted beliefs, especially in religion.

ex.en: The village was known for its strict orthodoxy and old customs.
ex.ko: 그 마을은 엄격한 정통 신앙과 옛 풍습으로 알려져 있었다.

easy: A small, round ball of something, like food or ice.

ex.en: I fed my rabbit a handful of food pellets.
ex.ko: 나는 토끼에게 사료 알갱이 한 줌을 주었다.

easy: The big bowl-shaped bones at your hips that your legs connect to.

ex.en: The skeleton in science class showed how the legs attach to the pelvis.
ex.ko: 과학 시간의 해골 모형은 다리가 골반에 어떻게 붙는지 보여 주었다.

easy: When light waves are made to shake in only one direction, like with special sunglasses.

ex.en: Polarization in my sunglasses cuts the glare from the lake.
ex.ko: 선글라스의 편광 덕분에 호수에서 반사되는 눈부심이 줄어든다.

easy: To stop people from doing something by using force or fear.

ex.en: The cruel ruler repressed anyone who spoke against him.
ex.ko: 잔인한 통치자는 자기에게 반대하는 사람을 모두 억압했다.

easy: A chemical in your brain that helps with sleep, mood, and memory.

ex.en: Playing outside in the sun may help your body make serotonin.
ex.ko: 햇볕 아래에서 밖에서 노는 것은 몸이 세로토닌을 만드는 데 도움이 될 수 있다.

easy: About sociology, the study of how people live and act together in groups.

ex.en: The sociological study looked at how families eat dinner together.
ex.ko: 그 사회학 연구는 가족이 함께 저녁을 먹는 방식을 살펴보았다.

easy: A club of female college students who often live together.

ex.en: My cousin joined a sorority in her first year of college.
ex.ko: 사촌 언니는 대학 1학년 때 여학생 사교 클럽에 들어갔다.

easy: A person who believes their own group of people is better than all others and should rule them.

ex.en: Dr. King spoke out against supremacists who treated people unfairly.
ex.ko: 킹 목사는 사람들을 부당하게 대하는 우월주의자들에게 맞서 목소리를 냈다.

easy: A young person who wants very much to become something, like a star or an expert.

ex.en: The talent show was full of singer wannabes hoping to be famous.
ex.ko: 장기 자랑 대회는 유명해지기를 꿈꾸는 가수 지망생들로 가득했다.

easy: Having a base chemical in it; the opposite of acid, with a pH higher than 7.

ex.en: Baking soda mixed with water makes an alkaline liquid.
ex.ko: 베이킹소다를 물에 섞으면 알칼리성 액체가 된다.

easy: The opening at the end of the body where poop comes out.

ex.en: Food travels through the intestines and leaves the body through the anus.
ex.ko: 음식은 장을 지나 항문을 통해 몸 밖으로 나간다.

easy: About arteries, the tubes that carry blood away from your heart.

ex.en: The doctor checked his arterial blood flow with a special machine.
ex.ko: 의사는 특별한 기계로 그의 동맥 혈류를 검사했다.

easy: To hurt or punish someone back because they did something bad to you or someone you love.

ex.en: In the movie, the young hero promised to avenge his father.
ex.ko: 영화에서 젊은 주인공은 아버지의 원수를 갚겠다고 맹세했다.

easy: A person who lives in the Balkan Peninsula in southeastern Europe.

ex.en: The Balkan farmer showed us how to make cheese.
ex.ko: 발칸 반도의 농부가 우리에게 치즈 만드는 법을 보여 주었다.

easy: A strong stretchy material in your skin, bones, and joints that holds your body together.

ex.en: Jelly is made from gelatin, which comes from collagen.
ex.ko: 젤리는 콜라겐에서 얻은 젤라틴으로 만든다.

easy: Very good; excellent.

ex.en: "That's a dandy idea!" said Grandpa about our lemonade stand.
ex.ko: "그거 아주 멋진 생각이구나!" 할아버지가 우리 레모네이드 가게를 두고 말씀하셨다.

easy: Retired from a job but allowed to keep the job's title as an honor.

ex.en: Grandpa is a professor emeritus, so he still visits the college sometimes.
ex.ko: 할아버지는 명예교수라서 지금도 가끔 대학에 가신다.

easy: A professor or minister who has retired but keeps the title as an honor.

ex.en: The emeritus gave a short speech at the science fair.
ex.ko: 명예교수가 과학 박람회에서 짧은 연설을 했다.

easy: A unit for measuring how deep water is; one fathom is 6 feet.

ex.en: The sailors found the water was ten fathoms deep.
ex.ko: 선원들은 물 깊이가 10패덤이라는 것을 알아냈다.

easy: To finally understand something that is hard to figure out.

ex.en: I can't fathom how the magician made the rabbit disappear.
ex.ko: 마술사가 토끼를 어떻게 사라지게 했는지 도무지 이해할 수가 없다.

easy: Extremely evil and wicked.

ex.en: Stealing from the children's hospital was a heinous crime.
ex.ko: 어린이 병원에서 물건을 훔친 것은 흉악한 범죄였다.

easy: When a doctor or other expert does their job badly or carelessly and someone gets hurt.

ex.en: The family said the doctor's mistake was malpractice.
ex.ko: 그 가족은 의사의 실수가 의료 과실이라고 말했다.

easy: Being new and up to date, belonging to the present time.

ex.en: The shiny glass library brought a feeling of modernity to our old town.
ex.ko: 반짝이는 유리 도서관은 오래된 우리 마을에 현대적인 느낌을 주었다.

easy: A chemical with nitrogen and oxygen in it, often used to help plants grow.

ex.en: Farmers put nitrates on fields so the corn grows tall.
ex.ko: 농부들은 옥수수가 크게 자라도록 밭에 질산염 비료를 준다.

easy: A very learned person who knows a lot about a subject.

ex.en: The pundit explained the history of the old temple to our class.
ex.ko: 그 학자는 우리 반에게 오래된 사원의 역사를 설명해 주었다.

easy: The time when someone rules in place of a king or queen who is too young or sick.

ex.en: During the regency, the young king's uncle made all the decisions.
ex.ko: 섭정 기간 동안 어린 왕의 삼촌이 모든 결정을 내렸다.

easy: In rugby, when players from both teams lock arms, push against each other, and try to get the ball.

ex.en: The players bent down and pushed hard in the scrum.
ex.ko: 선수들은 몸을 숙이고 스크럼에서 힘껏 밀었다.

easy: One of several layers lying on top of each other, like layers of rock.

ex.en: We saw a stratum of red rock in the canyon wall.
ex.ko: 우리는 협곡 벽에서 붉은 암석층을 보았다.

easy: A big, round yellow root vegetable, like a turnip.

ex.en: Grandma mashed the swede with butter for dinner.
ex.ko: 할머니는 저녁으로 루타바가를 버터와 함께 으깨 주셨다.

easy: News stories that try to shock people with gossip and exciting headlines instead of facts.

ex.en: The tabloid said a movie star had a pet alien.
ex.ko: 그 타블로이드 신문은 한 영화배우가 외계인을 애완동물로 키운다고 썼다.

easy: A person born when the sun is in the star sign Taurus, the bull (late April to May).

ex.en: My mom is a Taurus because her birthday is on May 5.
ex.ko: 엄마는 생일이 5월 5일이라서 황소자리다.

easy: An army vehicle with thick metal sides that carries soldiers safely.

ex.en: Soldiers climbed out of the armored personnel carrier.
ex.ko: 병사들이 병력 수송 장갑차에서 내렸다.

easy: A person whose job is to help keep people healthy or take care of sick people.

ex.en: The caregiver helped Grandma take her medicine every morning.
ex.ko: 돌보미가 매일 아침 할머니가 약을 드시도록 도와주었다.

easy: A thin, bendy tube that doctors put into the body to let liquid in or out.

ex.en: The nurse used a catheter to give the patient medicine.
ex.ko: 간호사는 카테터로 환자에게 약을 넣었다.

easy: Agreed to by everyone involved.

ex.en: The kids made a consensual choice to play tag first.
ex.ko: 아이들은 먼저 술래잡기를 하기로 서로 합의했다.

easy: An accountant who has passed hard tests and has a license to check money records and do taxes.

ex.en: Mom asked a CPA to help with our family's taxes.
ex.ko: 엄마는 우리 가족 세금 문제를 공인회계사에게 도와 달라고 했다.

easy: A group of chemicals, some of which are very strong poisons.

ex.en: The detective found that the poison in the story was cyanide.
ex.ko: 탐정은 이야기 속 독이 시안화물이라는 것을 알아냈다.

easy: No longer close or friendly with someone you used to be close to.

ex.en: The two estranged brothers finally hugged at the wedding.
ex.ko: 사이가 멀어졌던 두 형제는 결혼식에서 마침내 껴안았다.

easy: Bright light that some things give off when special light, like black light, shines on them.

ex.en: The poster glowed with fluorescence under the black light.
ex.ko: 포스터가 블랙라이트 아래에서 형광으로 빛났다.

easy: Old Celtic languages spoken in Ireland and Scotland.

ex.en: My Irish friend can say "hello" in Gaelic.
ex.ko: 내 아일랜드 친구는 게일어로 "안녕"이라고 말할 수 있다.

easy: A small ape with very long arms and no tail that swings through trees in Asia.

ex.en: The gibbon swung from branch to branch at the zoo.
ex.ko: 동물원에서 긴팔원숭이가 이 나뭇가지에서 저 나뭇가지로 매달려 옮겨 다녔다.

easy: Seeming harmless or pleasant, but slowly causing harm.

ex.en: Too much screen time can be insidious, slowly taking over your free time.
ex.ko: 화면을 너무 오래 보는 것은 모르는 사이에 자유 시간을 다 빼앗아 갈 수 있다.

easy: The group that is in charge of the Olympic Games.

ex.en: The IOC chose the city that will host the next Olympics.
ex.ko: 국제 올림픽 위원회가 다음 올림픽을 열 도시를 정했다.

easy: Special words that a certain group of people use and others may not understand.

ex.en: Skateboarders have their own lingo for tricks.
ex.ko: 스케이트보더들은 기술을 부르는 그들만의 은어가 있다.

easy: In India, a word for the number one hundred thousand (100,000).

ex.en: The movie made ten lakh rupees on its first day.
ex.ko: 그 영화는 첫날 100만 루피를 벌었다.

easy: About planning and moving people and things to the right place at the right time.

ex.en: Moving the whole school to a new building was a big logistical job.
ex.ko: 학교 전체를 새 건물로 옮기는 일은 계획과 운반이 많이 필요한 큰 일이었다.

easy: The first people of New Zealand, who came from Polynesia long ago.

ex.en: The Maori dancers performed the haka before the game.
ex.ko: 마오리족 무용수들이 경기 전에 하카 춤을 추었다.

easy: A big ocean fish with a long, pointed nose like a spear.

ex.en: The fisherman caught a huge marlin that leaped out of the water.
ex.ko: 어부는 물 위로 펄쩍 뛰어오른 거대한 청새치를 잡았다.

easy: Being someone's father.

ex.en: The test showed the paternity of the baby elephant at the zoo.
ex.ko: 검사로 동물원 아기 코끼리의 아빠가 누구인지 밝혀졌다.

easy: Of a family or society where the father or men are in charge.

ex.en: Long ago, many families were patriarchal, and the father made every rule.
ex.ko: 옛날에는 많은 가정이 가부장적이어서 아버지가 모든 규칙을 정했다.

easy: A heavy, silvery radioactive metal used in nuclear power and bombs.

ex.en: Plutonium is so dangerous that workers handle it with robot arms.
ex.ko: 플루토늄은 너무 위험해서 작업자들은 로봇 팔로 다룬다.

easy: A serious illness of the mind that makes it hard to tell what is real.

ex.en: With the right medicine, the man recovered from his psychosis.
ex.ko: 알맞은 약 덕분에 그 남자는 정신병에서 회복되었다.

easy: A deadly disease that animals can pass to people by biting.

ex.en: Our dog gets a shot every year so she can't catch rabies.
ex.ko: 우리 개는 광견병에 걸리지 않도록 해마다 주사를 맞는다.

easy: The amount of food each person gets for one day, especially soldiers.

ex.en: Each hiker carried a ration of trail mix and dried fruit.
ex.ko: 등산객마다 견과류와 말린 과일로 된 하루치 식량을 챙겼다.

easy: To let people have only a small, fixed amount of something because there is not enough.

ex.en: During the war, sugar was rationed, so each family got only a little.
ex.ko: 전쟁 중에는 설탕이 배급제여서 가족마다 조금씩만 받았다.

easy: Needed for something; necessary.

ex.en: She had all the requisite tools to build the birdhouse.
ex.ko: 그녀는 새집을 만드는 데 필요한 도구를 모두 가지고 있었다.

easy: Something you must have; something necessary.

ex.en: Water and a tent are requisites for a camping trip.
ex.ko: 물과 텐트는 캠핑 여행의 필수품이다.

easy: To bring someone or something back to life.

ex.en: In the fairy tale, a magic potion resurrected the sleeping prince.
ex.ko: 동화에서 마법의 물약이 잠든 왕자를 되살렸다.

easy: A hot sandwich with corned beef, Swiss cheese, and sauerkraut on rye bread.

ex.en: Dad ordered a Reuben at the deli, and it was stuffed with meat.
ex.ko: 아빠가 델리에서 루벤 샌드위치를 시켰는데 고기가 가득 들어 있었다.

easy: In a fair way that is deserved.

ex.en: The trophy rightfully belongs to the team that won the most games.
ex.ko: 트로피는 당연히 가장 많이 이긴 팀의 것이다.

easy: To make someone feel sad.

ex.en: The news that our teacher was moving away saddened the whole class.
ex.ko: 선생님이 이사 간다는 소식에 반 전체가 슬퍼했다.

easy: To put different things together to make something new.

ex.en: Plants synthesize sugar from sunlight, water, and air.
ex.ko: 식물은 햇빛과 물, 공기로 당분을 합성한다.

easy: A time when you stay awake all night, often to watch or wait.

ex.en: The family kept a vigil by the sick puppy's bed.
ex.ko: 가족은 아픈 강아지 곁에서 밤을 새웠다.

easy: A Latin word for year, used in "per annum," meaning each year.

ex.en: The club fee is twenty dollars per annum.
ex.ko: 동아리 회비는 1년에 20달러이다.

easy: A white powder that is a strong poison, once used to kill rats.

ex.en: Long ago, people used arsenic to get rid of rats.
ex.ko: 옛날 사람들은 쥐를 없애려고 비소를 썼다.

easy: A person who gives money to help a plan or project.

ex.en: The school play found a backer who paid for the costumes.
ex.ko: 학교 연극은 의상비를 내 줄 후원자를 찾았다.

easy: A very poor person who lives by asking others for money or food.

ex.en: The kind baker gave bread to the beggar every morning.
ex.ko: 친절한 제빵사는 매일 아침 거지에게 빵을 주었다.

easy: Old and silly, used so often that it is no longer interesting.

ex.en: Dad's corny jokes make us groan, but we still laugh.
ex.ko: 아빠의 식상한 농담에 우리는 끙 소리를 내지만 그래도 웃는다.

easy: Leaving out a sound or word when you speak, like the silent "d" in "sandwich."

ex.en: Many people say "sanwich" because of the deletion of the "d" sound.
ex.ko: 많은 사람이 "d" 소리를 빼고 "샌위치"라고 발음한다.

easy: A person who works and gets paid money.

ex.en: Mom is the main earner in our family.
ex.ko: 엄마가 우리 집에서 주로 돈을 버는 사람이다.

easy: Breaking something into many tiny pieces.

ex.en: The fragmentation of the rock made fine sand.
ex.ko: 바위가 잘게 부서져서 고운 모래가 되었다.

easy: A US government group that makes sure businesses play fair and do not trick shoppers.

ex.en: The FTC stopped the company from making false claims about its toys.
ex.ko: 미국 연방거래위원회는 그 회사가 장난감에 대해 거짓 광고를 하지 못하게 막았다.

easy: To praise someone or something very highly.

ex.en: The song glorifies the brave firefighters who saved the town.
ex.ko: 그 노래는 마을을 구한 용감한 소방관들을 칭송한다.

easy: A German word used before a man's name, like "Mr." in English.

ex.en: Herr Weber is our new German teacher.
ex.ko: 베버 씨가 우리 새 독일어 선생님이다.

easy: The chemical symbol for mercury, a silver metal that is liquid at room temperature.

ex.en: On the periodic table, Hg stands for mercury.
ex.ko: 주기율표에서 Hg는 수은을 나타낸다.

easy: A person paid to try to get lawmakers to vote a certain way.

ex.en: The lobbyist met with senators to talk about the new park law.
ex.ko: 로비스트는 새 공원 법에 대해 이야기하려고 상원 의원들을 만났다.

easy: A US government group that studies the oceans and the air and forecasts the weather.

ex.en: NOAA warned everyone that a hurricane was coming.
ex.ko: 미국 국립해양대기청은 허리케인이 오고 있다고 모두에게 경고했다.

easy: The main kind of money in Uruguay.

ex.en: We paid fifty pesos for ice cream in Montevideo.
ex.ko: 우리는 몬테비데오에서 아이스크림 값으로 50페소를 냈다.

easy: Having to do with how things or people are connected.

ex.en: The puzzle tests relational thinking, like who is taller than whom.
ex.ko: 그 퍼즐은 누가 누구보다 키가 큰지 같은 관계를 생각하는 능력을 시험한다.

easy: Pulling you in and making you want to do something.

ex.en: The seductive smell of fresh cookies pulled me into the kitchen.
ex.ko: 갓 구운 쿠키의 유혹적인 냄새에 나는 부엌으로 끌려갔다.
